2026-09-10T12:39:30.3399255Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3399684Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3400063Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3400812Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3401299Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3401882Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3403571Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3405479Z >
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3409356Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3413590Z >
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3414560Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3415403Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3415636Z ### How to Use
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3415924Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3416750Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3417699Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3417926Z ```bash
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3418650Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3419515Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3420439Z ```
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3420737Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3421077Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3421729Z ```bash
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3423966Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3424920Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3426024Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3426898Z ```
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3427147Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3428980Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3430043Z ```bash
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3430944Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3431746Z ```
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3432092Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3432531Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3433512Z ```bash
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3434155Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3435161Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3435972Z ```
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3436227Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3436555Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3437038Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3438574Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3440482Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3440713Z ```bash
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3441252Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3442251Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3443214Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3443612Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3444181Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3445343Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3446285Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3446847Z ```
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3447104Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3447953Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3449637Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3449874Z ```bash
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3450988Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3453314Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3454295Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3454804Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3455311Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3456253Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3456927Z ```
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3457183Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3457437Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3458389Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3459523Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3460852Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3462052Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3463359Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3463980Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3464201Z ### Notes
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3464469Z 
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3468986Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3471114Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3472558Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3473983Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3475364Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3476693Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3477814Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-09-10T12:39:30.3478632Z </mcp-clis>
